result.title: Think with Skills: Pseudocode Planning Before Execution for Advanced Reasoners
result.summary: Language model agents often struggle with complex tasks even when equipped with expert-written skills. Such skills encode declarative knowledge, whereas successful execution requires procedural knowledge tailored to the task at hand. Natural language skills may leave conditions and dependencies implicit, and tasks involving multiple skills further require agents to coordinate intermediate results and execution order. We introduce Think with Skills, a method that trains reasoning models to turn relevant skill descriptions into task-specific pseudocode plans before execution. The pseudocode explicitly represents operations, conditions, intermediate results, and dependencies, providing a structured bridge from skill descriptions to agent actions. We construct training data that pairs tasks and skills with pseudocode plans and execution trajectories, use supervised fine tuning to initialize this behavior, and further optimize end-to-end task performance with Group Relative Policy Optimization. On SkillsBench, Think with Skills raises task success from 35.0% to 62.0%. These results show that proceduralizing expert knowledge before execution substantially improves skill use.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Think with Skills：训练推理模型在执行前把给定技能描述转写为任务特定的伪代码计划，显式写出操作、条件、中间结果与依赖关系，并用 SFT 初始化该行为、再用 GRPO 端到端优化，在 SkillsBench 上将任务成功率从 35.0% 提升到 62.0%。
AI.relevance_reason: 以显式伪代码充当执行前的结构化中间状态，并配合 SFT+RL 监督，可能为 LVR 中「中间状态应承载何种任务必要信息、如何训练其被后续步骤真正使用」提供可核查线索；但属纯文本 agent 技能编排，与视觉证据和 latent 状态生成无直接关系。
